reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identified the two stoichiometries and the RcpA-TadD binding interface as the principal novel discoveries; the final paper reports both the C13/C14 assemblies and the C-terminal RcpA interaction with TadD.

The reviewer noted that fitting the RcpA segment in the TadD groove was challenging and requested clearer structural support. The final paper still states that map resolution was insufficient to identify the interface residues unequivocally, although truncation and cross-linking provide supporting evidence.

The reviewer specifically highlighted the combination of focused cryo-EM classification, light microscopy, and cross-linking with controls. The final paper documents these complementary data streams for the structural and functional conclusions.

The reviewer described the biochemical and fluorescence experiments as establishing TadD-dependent RcpA oligomerization and interaction determinants. The final paper reports direct association, native-cell colocalization, C-terminal truncation, and cysteine cross-linking evidence.

The original concern was the credibility of the RcpA density assignment in the TadD groove. Final text provides experimental validation but explicitly retains the limitation that map resolution alone could not unequivocally assign the residues.

The reviewer asked whether a 13/14-mer RcpA N-domain model had been made. The final paper reports an unresolved N-domain, an AlphaFold monomeric model, and a proposed VirB9-like ring, leaving its organization and function open.

The request for broader and clearer pilotin context is audit-only: the final introduction describes non-conserved pilotin architectures, distinct assembly/localization roles, and systems using inner-membrane assembly platforms.
The boiling and SDS-resistance clarification is audit-only: the final Methods state that samples were not heated before electrophoresis and describe the effect of heating on the oligomeric state.

The figure-7 interpretability concern is audit-only: the final figure legend identifies lysate and elution lanes, antibody readouts, replicate number, particle counts, and controls for the truncation and cross-linking experiments.
The figure-8 component and localization concern is audit-only: the final schematic includes TadZ and its legend explains the basis for depicting RcpC in both membrane fractions.
The request to show C14 particles is audit-only: the final paper presents C14 class averages and reports their frequency in both heterologous and native-expression preparations.
The Fig. 4b gel-identification concern is audit-only: the final figure legend identifies the antistrep Western blot and the native-expression purification context.
The apparent monomeric RcpA band in the fluorescent strain cannot be fully reconciled from the final-paper span alone; it remains audit-only and does not support a retained review point.

limiting_points.text: The interface assignment is constrained by the focused map: the paper states that its resolution could not unequivocally identify the RcpA residues in the TadD groove, so the structural interpretation depends on convergent truncation and cross-linking evidence.

supporting_points.text: The study establishes a structurally and functionally supported RcpA-TadD interaction and identifies C13 and C14 secretin-pilotin assemblies, extending structural understanding of the Tad secretion system.

questions.text: The organization and role of the flexible RcpA N-domain remain open: it was not resolved experimentally, while the proposed VirB9-like periplasmic ring is based on AlphaFold and homologous architecture.

strengths.text: Focused cryo-EM classification is integrated with cellular colocalization, biochemical assembly assays, and targeted cysteine cross-linking, providing independent evidence for the proposed RcpA-TadD mechanism.

The functional link is tested across complementary perturbations: loss of the RcpA C terminus disrupts TadD recruitment and secretin assembly, while paired cysteine substitutions restore assembly and yield the predicted cross-linked products.

summary.text: This study defines the Pseudomonas aeruginosa RcpA-TadD outer-membrane secretin-pilotin complex using cryo-EM, cellular localization, biochemical assembly assays, and cysteine cross-linking. It reports C13 and C14 assemblies and places the RcpA C terminus in the TadD groove as a determinant of complex formation. The retained limitation is that the focused density does not by itself assign the interface residues unequivocally, and the flexible RcpA N-domain remains structurally unresolved.

weaknesses.text: Although the C-terminal RcpA-TadD contact is supported by truncation and cross-linking, the final paper acknowledges that the focused cryo-EM map was insufficient for unequivocal residue identification; the atomic placement at the interface therefore remains partially constrained.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The final introduction supplies the requested broader pilotin and secretin context.
The final Methods clarify unboiled sample handling and the heat-resistant oligomer.
The final Figure 7 legend supplies lane, assay, control, and replication information.
The final Figure 8 schematic includes TadZ and documents the RcpC localization rationale.
C14 class averages and their occurrence are reported in the final paper.
The Fig. 4b legend identifies the antistrep Western blot and native purification context.
The final-paper evidence does not fully establish the cause of the monomeric band in the fluorescent strain.
